system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller labels such as **“STANDARD”, “FINAL” and “agreed” are not evidence of Buyer approval**. The review below treats all positions as negotiable. It relies on the supplied extracts, not independent review of DD-002–DD-012 or the complete SPA.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery calibrated to diligence risks, with separate treatment for fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims. | **Counter at 50% (AUD 12m)** as a negotiating position; accept a lower general cap only against adequate separate protections—20% may leave material losses uninsured. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for separately protected claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated—the current combination leaves substantial losses with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties; separate longer periods for other categories and effective preservation of notified contingent claims. | **Seek 36 months, with 24 months a potential fallback**, and reject universal application—latent issues may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering authority, ownership, all issued shares and absence of encumbrances; no thresholds; at least price-level cap and longer survival. | **Require a separate AUD 24m cap and seek seven-year survival**, coordinated with execution form and applicable limitation law—ownership risk should not consume or be constrained by the general warranty allowance. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation remedies, including appropriate attribution of representatives’ conduct. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy/non-reliance restrictions**, preserving non-excludable rights—fraud must not benefit from contractual liability shields. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of indexed data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; a fixed, retained disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific warranty-linked disclosures**, with narrowly identified general disclosures if negotiated—document availability is not adequate explanation of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion, particularly no constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete; fallback only to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, with Seller bearing proof**, excluding protected claim categories—the draft effectively transfers diligence and disclosure risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied upon delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of associated conditions supplied. | Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent and satisfaction of relevant clause 11.3 conditions without unacceptable amendments or costs. | **Do not complete until consent and its conditions are verified**, with a long-stop/termination right—approximately **30% of revenue** is exposed, and a consent document alone may be insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment at Completion and effective security discharge through binding completion arrangements; correct debt deduction. | **Require payout letter, direct repayment and effective release arrangements at Completion**, with filing evidence afterwards if necessary—Buyer must receive the agreed debt-free business without continuing security exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller-funded bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with payment responsibility and price treatment explicit. | **Include verified amounts and on-costs in completion funding/debt-like adjustments or an equivalent Seller-funded mechanism**, backed by an indemnity and no double counting—omission could leave Buyer funding transaction-triggered liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without independent payment verification or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership transfer; protection against ownership defects, third-party claims and resulting remediation losses. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment at Completion, plus a broader standalone indemnity and appropriate retention**—paying an invoice alone may not resolve the IP ownership and exploitation risk. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal notification assessment and allocation of pre-Completion incident costs. | **Require investigation updates and remediation covenants, plus a specific indemnity and proportionate security**, covering legally recoverable losses—the uncertainty warrants protection, not a finding that a breach or notification duty is already established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Combined review of **AUD 330,000**, timing, services, termination rights, accruals and any pre-Completion commitment restrictions. | **Reserve treatment pending DD-008/DD-011 review; adjust or indemnify only where justified, without double counting**—neither ordinary-course treatment nor a full price deduction is established by the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless excluded. | Distinct regimes for general, fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant and payment/adjustment claims; fraud separately protected. | **Rewrite definitions and operative cross-references with express category exclusions and priority rules**—otherwise blanket language can neutralise negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller owns 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, transfers/allotments, beneficial ownership, encumbrances, options and other rights to acquire shares. | **Verify the register against corporate records and relevant searches; obtain transfer documents, releases and fundamental warranties**—the register is important evidence but does not alone resolve every title or dilution risk. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranty terms said to be settled within the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with suitable assessment-period survival; robust IP warranties and tailored protection for known defects. | **Keep both open: seek seven-year tax protection, longer where assessment exposure warrants, and risk-specific IP caps/survival plus the Ironquay indemnity**—tax and core-IP exposure should not default to an 18-month, 20% recovery regime. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent and conditions; Riverlark repayment/release; Seller-funded bonuses; and verified Ironquay IP transfer. Disclosure of these matters is **not** a substitute for resolving them or allocating their economic risk expressly.
=== END ADVICE ===
